File colour

Rules

  • Primary logo is the logotype on its own.
  • Clear space around the logo equals the height of the letter h. Keep it free of text and graphics.
  • The H icon works alone for avatars, favicons and small sizes.
  • The icon doubles as a seal: debossed on cartons, stamped in Clay on tissue, envelopes and shipping boxes.
  • Never rotate, stretch, outline, shadow or set the logo in another font.
  • Never place it on a colour outside the palette, or on an image where it stops being legible.
  • Never put the analemma inside a lockup. It is a brand device, not a logo element.
  • Never stamp the seal in Umber. Seal ink is Clay.

The analemma

The shape the sun draws over one place photographed at the same hour across a year, calculated for Seoul. One dot per recorded morning. It prints in gold foil on packaging.

  • Packaging, social and campaign work only.
  • The loop stays asymmetric. Never regularised into a figure-eight.
  • Never used as a product name or an SEO term.

Files

Set up Canva

Ten minutes once, and every future post starts on brand.

  1. Open Brand, then Brand Kits, and create one called Haetsal.
  2. Upload the logo files from the assets folder, including the reversed versions.
  3. Add the five palette colours by pasting each HEX. Name them Paper, Almond, Clay, Apricot, Umber.
  4. Upload the fonts and set Suisse Int'l medium as heading, regular as body. Keep Perfectly Nineties for the logo only.
  5. Delete every default colour and font Canva added, so nobody picks one by accident.

Font upload needs Canva Pro. Without it, keep the logo as an image and set headings in the closest neutral grotesque Canva offers.

Brand Brain

Copy this into a Claude Project or a custom GPT, and everything written inside it follows the brand: voice, rules, colour, type, image world. Ask for a product description, an email or a set of captions, and it checks itself against the brand before it answers.

The full brand instruction file
Paste into project instructions, or custom instructions, and save.

Image prompts

Set this up once and you stop uploading anything. In Higgsfield open Elements, in another tool its saved references, and save each file from the References folder under exactly these names:

  1. product and box, the current tube and carton render. The files are already named this way.
  2. model-01 to model-06, one element per face. Where two files share a number (model-01-a, model-01-b) they are the same woman from two angles, feed both into that one element.
  3. Nothing else. No new faces, no old pack renders.

From then on the prompts below run as written: type @product or @model-03 and the image comes in on its own. In a tool without saved references, attach the matching file instead of the handle, model first, product second.

The product never changes, the model does. The pack, the palette and the label are identical in every image, which is why every prompt ends with the same lock line. Swap @model-0X for a different face, model-01 through model-06, shot by shot so a feed does not read as one woman's diary, and never put two of them in one image. Never ask the tool to invent a face.

If the label garbles or a colour shifts, cut the prompt back to the first sentence plus the light and the lock line, then add one sentence at a time until it breaks. Run each prompt a few times and pick.
